messages:
amy: Heads-up — after the canary deploy at 11:14 we saw sustained compile activity and 3x tail latency on short-seq workloads. graphs: https://internal/graphs/2351234567 :grimacing:
rafa: saw the same, repro on canary-3. Compiles/sec jumped from ~10 -> 220 for kernel variants.
morgan: infra-bot reported compile-queue depth spike, plus a bunch of KVS invalidation logs for redwood-3b-seq128.
infra-bot: [deploy] rollout canary/2026-03-17T11:12 by @kevin — 3 hosts updated.
kevin: rolled the heuristic change from PR #4567 (autotune: increase score weight for new short-seq kernel). merged this morning.
amy: quick logs (truncated):
```
[2026-03-17T11:15:02Z] compile_queue.enqueue kernel=tch_attn_small seq_len=32 model=redwood-3b id=0x7f9
[2026-03-17T11:15:02Z] compile start kernel=tch_attn_small->tch_attn_v2 opt_level=3
[2026-03-17T11:15:02Z] kvcache.invalidate model=redwood-3b seq_prefix=0..128 reason=kernel_change
[2026-03-17T11:15:04Z] compile finish kernel=tch_attn_v2 compile_time=1.8s
[2026-03-17T11:15:05Z] runtime.request slow path: waiting for compile id=0x7f9
```
rafa: key bit — kvcache.invalidate due to kernel_change. We rely on prefix/KV reuse for short-seq clients; if we invalidate aggressively we blow up token cost and trigger compiles.
morgan: CI perf windows did show a tiny regression in the autotune unit test last night (0.8% latency), but it was under the threshold and got merged. looks like in prod it amplifies because of request pattern.
kevin: hypothesis: autotune scoring bump prefers tch_attn_v2 for seq_len<=64, but new kernel has different kv-storage layout -> invalidation key mismatch -> cache dropout -> many cold requests -> compile storm for fallback variants.
amy: repro steps I used: spin up canary vm, hit /generate with seq 16 5qps from 50 clients, observe compile queue. sharing a short repro script.
```
# repro sketch
for i in $(seq 1 50); do
  curl -sS -X POST https://canary-3/api/generate -d '{"seq_len":16, "prompt":"hi"}' &
done
```
rafa: workaround: flip feature flag autotune.short_seq_weight back to previous value (rollout flag). We can toggle quickly with /feature toggle.
morgan: confirmed toggle reduces compiles within 60s on the canary. But we still have some KVs dropped; need to prevent aggressive invalidation on schema-level changes.
kevin: I'm going to open a revert PR in case the toggle isn't sufficient for prod. planning: revert #4567 -> monitor for 2 hours -> gradual re-apply with canary-only heuristic. assigning @kevin to revert, @rafa to monitor compile queue, @morgan to audit KV invalidation causal path.
kevin: created PR #4578 revert of #4567. command: `gh pr create --repo redwood/inference --title "revert: autotune short-seq weight" --body "revert PR #4567 due to compile/KV invalidation spike"`
amy: adding perf traces and flamegraphs to the PR. attaching perf dump: /artifacts/2351234567/perf.tar.gz
rafa: small note — the kernel selection logic uses a seeded tiebreaker. the seed we chose changed between canary and prod builds (build time random) which explains slightly different picks across hosts. should unify seed or make deterministic.
morgan: also found that compile cache TTL is 10m and gets evicted under memory pressure; with the invalidation above we race with TTL and regen compiles repeatedly. suggest bump TTL to 60m while we stabilize.
kevin: summary + immediate actions:
- revert PR #4567 (in progress) — KEVIN
- toggle autotune.short_seq_weight to old value on prod flag set — KEVIN/MORGAN
- monitor compile-queue and latency dashboards for 2x hours — RAFA
- run targeted unit + e2e perf tests with seq_len=16,32 patterns to validate — AMY
- root cause followup: make kvcache invalidation schema-change-safe + unify autotune seed — MORGAN/RAFA
amy: if revert looks good we'll do a hotfix release and then rework heuristic with deterministic seed + no KV schema churn. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: [alert] compile-queue depth returned to baseline at 11:56 on canary-3.
rafa: looks like toggle + partial revert dropped compiles back to normal. still want the hotfix for TTL and seed fixes before full rollout.
kevin: I'm going to hold the prod rollout until we have the seed deterministic work scheduled. assigning follow-ups as JIRA tickets.
amy: thanks everyone — creating postmortem draft, will ping for reviews.
__notes: Generated Slack thread JSON for eng-runtime about a kernel selection/compilation heuristic regression, compile storm and KV cache invalidation. All fields are strings or list of strings as required.
